structure: Part 1 read how the live-animals set is mounted and sequenced, not what its pages say. It read in full: src/server/app/routes.js and routes-live-animals.js (the Hapi plugin that mounts the set and the order it configures its seams in); the generic flow layer src/server/app/flow/ (dispatch.js, gates.js, prerequisites.js, navigation.js, journey-flow.js, section-status.js); the set's identity sets/live-animals/set.js and its journey config journeys/linear/config.js; the composition files journeys/linear/features/index.js (28 route bundles, 15 dispatch pages), features/evaluation.js and features/system/evaluation.js; the whole of journeys/linear/flow/ (flow.js's 8 sections, task-rows.js's 12 rows, entry-guard.js, stored-answers.js, notification-action-slugs.js, section-captions/index.js with copy.en.js and copy.cy.js, fixtures/happy-path.json, and reachability-fixtures/seeds.js, scope-states.js and enumerate-answer-states.js); all 12 obligation files (obligations/index.js plus the 11 section files, commodities/identifiers.js, lines.js and aggregates.js among them); the eight files of sets/live-animals/services/commodities/; and the two test-support files (sets/live-animals/test-support.js, journeys/linear/test-support.js). To ground facts those files rest on it also read, outside its own list: shared/paths.js (the URL builders), bridge/obligation-source.js (SYSTEM_POPULATED, ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE), bridge/status/index.js and bridge/status/vocabulary.js (statusOf and the five statuses), the seven gate helpers under model/obligations/helpers/, obligation-purity.js and set-completeness.js (the boot assertions), each dispatch page's `collects` from its controller.js and each flow page's id, slug, subPage and maturity from its page.js, shared/kit.js's CYA_SLUG and CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG, features/transport/transporter-add-session.js and features/commodities/search/selection/rows.js (the flow-only key values), services/reference-data/request.js, common/services/mode.js and common/helpers/frontend-url.js. It covers: the set base, id and the URL shape every page hangs off; the 28 route bundles and which pages the flow holds that declare no obligations; how a page claims an obligation and how a derived page or section gate is worked out; the 8 journey sections in order with their pages and the review section's gate; all 12 task rows with their parts, conditions and how rowStatus decides; the two answers enforced at Save and continue and where a trader lands without them; the entry guard and the INS type-question URL; the 9 section captions verbatim in English with Welsh key parity; the 6 flow-only keys; all 52 obligations with their level, mandate, scope condition and cardinality; and the commodity reference service with its code lists, species check and stub. It claims no page's own heading, caption position, fields, hints, options or error messages: each feature's part does that.

claims.statement: Every request into the set enters the set's context before authentication runs, and every route is wrapped so it runs in that context.
claims.note: mechanism: carries the ambient set id through a request so set-keyed stores (dispatch index, journey flow, obligations, records, session) resolve to this set.

claims.statement: The entry guard runs before every handler in the set and, when it names a target, redirects there and stops the request.
The set refuses to mount when it has left any required seam unconfigured, naming each one.
The set refuses to mount when any of its journey cookies was not registered on the server.
Boot refuses an obligation model that carries any display key, such as a label, title or hint: display wording may not live in the obligation model.
Boot refuses the set when two pages both claim to collect the same obligation, naming the obligation and both pages.
Boot refuses the set when any obligation that is not system-populated is collected by no page, naming each uncovered obligation.
An obligation id may not contain a path metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']'), and boot refuses one that does.
claims.quote:
const ID_UNSAFE = /[.[\]]/
...
      throw new Error(
        `Obligation id "${obligation.name}" (at ${templatePath}) contains a path ` +
          `metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']') — ids must be path-safe`
      )

claims.statement: Boot also refuses the set when a feature's fulfilment bindings do not cover every obligation, and when a party binding is not scalar.

claims.note: The assertion names say what they refuse; the assertion bodies live in bridge/fulfilment-registry.js and features/addresses/assert-party-bindings.js, outside this part's slice.

claims.statement: A page claims an obligation by naming it in the `collects` list on the page's meta, and the page that claims a group also owns every obligation nested inside it, because ownership is resolved by walking up the obligation's dotted path to the nearest claimed ancestor.

    'regionOfOriginCode',
    'internalReferenceNumber'
  ],
  validation
}

The review section holds three pages in order, the notification view, the declaration and the confirmation, and opens only when the journey is ready for check your answers.

claims.statement: A journey is ready for check your answers when every task row leaves the trader nothing to do, that is when each row reads fulfilled, not applicable or optional.
claims.quote:
/** True for a status that leaves nothing for the trader to do: fulfilled, not
 * applicable or optional. */
export const rowReady = (status) =>
  status === FULFILLED || status === NA || status === OPTIONAL

export const readyForCheckYourAnswers = (answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  journeyTaskRows().every((row) =>
    rowReady(journeyRowStatus(row, answers, inScope, evaluation))
  )

claims.statement: The answer sections are the seven sections other than review, so a section list used for answering excludes the review.

A section with no authored gate opens when its prerequisite answers are all given and at least one obligation its pages collect is in scope; a section whose pages collect nothing opens unconditionally.
claims.quote:
const prerequisitesMet = (prerequisiteIds, scope) =>
  prerequisiteIds.every((id) => scope.answered(id))

const inScopeReachable = (obligationIds, scope) =>
  obligationIds.length === 0 ||
  obligationIds.some((id) => scope.inScope.has(id))
...
  return (
    prerequisitesMet(sectionPrerequisites(section), scope) &&
    inScopeReachable(sectionObligationIds(section), scope)
  )

claims.statement: A page with no authored gate applies when at least one obligation it collects is in scope; a page that collects nothing always applies.
An authored gate on a page replaces both the derived scope test and the required-earlier-answer test, so a page that states its own gate is never held back for a missing earlier answer.
claims.quote:
const prerequisitesAllowPage = (page, scope) =>
  Boolean(page.gate) || earliestMissingAnswerPage(page.id, scope) === undefined

export const pageGatePasses = (page, scope) =>
  prerequisitesAllowPage(page, scope) && pageAppliesTo(page, scope)

claims.statement: A section's prerequisite answers are those of its first page, so a section is held back by the same earlier answers its first page needs.
Exactly two answers are enforced at Save and continue, the country of origin and the commodity code, and they are the only answers a later page can be held back for.
claims.quote:
export const ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE = new Set([
  'countryOfOrigin',
  'commodityCode'
])

claims.statement: A page is held back only by those enforced answers whose own page comes earlier than it in the journey's page order, so an enforced answer asked later in the flow never blocks an earlier page.
claims.quote:
const continueOwnersBefore = (flowIndex) =>
  continueObligationOwners().filter(
    (owner) => owner.flowIndex !== -1 && owner.flowIndex < flowIndex
  )

const continuePrereqsBefore = (flowIndex) =>
  continueOwnersBefore(flowIndex).map((owner) => owner.id)

claims.statement: When a trader reaches a page whose required earlier answers are missing, they are sent to the page that asks for the earliest missing one in page order, and the page they tried to open is recorded with every missing answer id.
Save and continue goes to the next page in journey order that applies to this consignment, skipping any page that does not apply.
claims.quote:
const next = pages
    .slice(index + 1)
    .filter(isStep)
    .find((page) => pageAppliesTo(page, scope))
  if (!next) {
    return undefined
  }

The CPH number and permanent address pages are marked as sub-pages, so Save and continue never lands on either of them even though both are in the journey's sections.
The permanent address page is in the journey's sections but in no task row, so it is reachable only from another page, not from the task list.

claims.statement: Past the last step of the journey, Save and continue has no next page to offer.
Pressing Save and continue on a page that is in no journey section raises an error naming the page.
A task row's link opens the first of its pages whose gate passes, and falls back to the row's first page when none does.
The task rows shown under a section are those whose first page sits in that section, ordered by where that page falls in the section.
claims.quote:
const firstPageIndexIn = (section, row) =>
  section.pages.findIndex((page) => page.id === row.pages[0].id)

export const taskRowsOfSection = (section) =>
  journeyTaskRows()
    .filter((row) => firstPageIndexIn(section, row) !== -1)
    .sort(
      (rowA, rowB) =>
        firstPageIndexIn(section, rowA) - firstPageIndexIn(section, rowB)
    )

claims.statement: A row's status is worked out in three steps: a row whose condition does not apply reads not applicable; otherwise the row's parts are rolled up into a status; and a rolled-up fulfilled is demoted to in progress when the row's extra answer is still missing.
A row that does not author its own parts counts the obligations its pages collect, so the task list follows the dispatch ownership map by default.
claims.quote:
export const rowParts = (row) =>
  row.parts ?? row.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

claims.statement: A task row or section reads as one of five statuses: not applicable, not started, in progress, fulfilled or optional.
claims.quote:
export const NA = 'not-applicable'
export const NOT_STARTED = 'not-started'
export const IN_PROGRESS = 'in-progress'
export const FULFILLED = 'fulfilled'
export const OPTIONAL = 'optional'

claims.statement: A row with nothing in scope reads not applicable; a row with no mandatory part reads optional while untouched, then fulfilled or in progress; and a row with mandatory parts reads fulfilled when each is satisfied, in progress when something is started, and not started otherwise.
An empty collection that is required still blocks a row from reading fulfilled, and an empty collection that is optional reads optional while a partly filled optional one reads in progress.
claims.quote:
so the presentation-facing edge cases (empty optional collection -> OPTIONAL,
 * partial optional -> IN_PROGRESS, empty required collection -> NOT_STARTED)
 * hold.
...
 * The empty-collection floor is manifest-sourced (`requiredAtLeastOne`:
 * `requires.minEntries` or `requires.anyOfIds`) and stays a presentation
 * rule — the model emits nothing for a group with zero records, but an
 * empty required collection must still block FULFILLED.

claims.statement: A section's status rolls up every obligation its pages collect, in page order.
claims.quote:
export const sectionObligationIds = (section) =>
  section.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

export const sectionStatus = (section, answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  statusOf(sectionObligationIds(section), answers, inScope, evaluation)

claims.statement: A task row whose already-saved answers no longer pass its own pages' rules is demoted back to 'To do' on the overview, however complete the engine counts it.
A row's stored-answer errors are its pages' stored-answer errors merged, and a page that states no rules of its own contributes none.
claims.note: mechanism: merges each page's stored-answer error map for one task row.

The entry guard applies to any page path under /live-animals/notifications/<journeyId>/ and leaves the create path, the four notification action paths and the origin page (with anything under it) alone.
A trader who opens a guarded page of a notification with no answer entered yet is sent to that notification's origin page.
That redirect is logged once at info with the notification's id and the path the trader asked for, under the message 'No answer entered, sent to the first page'.

claims.statement: A notification counts as having committed answers when any stored key is a trader-entered obligation (not a system-populated one) and holds an answer; a flow-only key such as the declaration does not count.
claims.note: A flow-only key is not in the obligation manifest, so obligationByName returns undefined for it.

claims.statement: The notification carries 52 obligations in all, listed in one manifest order that runs from the system reference number through origin, import reason, parties, transport, arrival, contact, commodity lines and identifiers to the accompanying documents.
claims.quote:
export const obligations = [
  poApprovedReferenceNumber,
  countryOfOrigin,
...
  documentUploadId,
  documentFilename
]

claims.statement: Three of the 52 obligations are groups that hold others inside them: the commodity lines, the animal identifier records inside a line, and the documents.
claims.note: commodityLine, unitRecord (animalIdentifiers) and documents are the only obligations named as another obligation's `within`.

claims.statement: The country of origin is always asked and always mandatory.
The country-of-origin subdivision code is always in scope and always optional.
Whether a region-of-origin code is required is itself always asked and mandatory.

The region-of-origin code is always in scope, and it switches from optional to mandatory when the trader answers yes to whether a region code is required; the reason given is that a region code is required.
claims.note: This is the only gate in the set that keeps an obligation in scope on both branches, so the answer is never purged when the requirement flips to no.

claims.statement: The arrival date at the port is always asked and always mandatory.
The port of entry is always asked and always mandatory.
The transporter type is always asked and always mandatory.
The commercial transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Commercial, and a stored commercial transporter is dropped when the type is switched away from Commercial.
The private transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Private, and goes out of scope otherwise.
The commercial and private transporter records are mutually exclusive: only one of the two can be in scope for any transporter type.
claims.quote: // Transporter type + mutually-exclusive address blocks

claims.statement: The means of transport is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport identification is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport document reference is always asked and always mandatory.

The countries transited are asked of rail and road consignments only, and even then they are never compulsory: a trader who passes through nowhere they can name leaves the list empty, the row reads Optional and submission is not held up.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the comment records it as a design release 1 decision.

claims.statement: A conditional obligation whose in-scope decision names no mandate is treated as mandatory, so an optional conditional answer must say 'optional' outright.
claims.quote:
// `status` must say 'optional' outright — `effectiveStatus` falls back to
// 'mandatory' for an implication that carries none.

claims.statement: The place of origin is always asked and always mandatory, and is stored as one composite address record.
The consignor is always asked and always mandatory.
The consignee is always asked and always mandatory.
The importer is always asked and always mandatory.
The place of destination is always asked and always mandatory.
The reason for import is always asked and always mandatory.
The purpose in the internal market is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is internalMarket, and any stored purpose is dropped when the reason changes.
The destination country is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or transhipmentOrOnwardTravel, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the code records the V4 data dictionary (Confluence page 6497338582) as the authority for this rule.

claims.statement: The port of exit is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is chosen from the same port list as the port of entry.
The exit date is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
The contact address is always asked and always mandatory.
The internal reference number is trader-entered, always in scope and always optional.
What the animals are certified for is asked once for the whole notification and is always mandatory, although the spec notes APHA may make it depend on the commodity later.
The notification's approved reference number is assigned by the system when the notification is created and is never entered by a trader; it is mandatory but no page asks for it.
The notification's reference number is shaped GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX, where the six-character body uses Crockford base32 (0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O or U).
A notification must hold at least one commodity line, and an empty list is refused under the code obligation.commodityLine.atLeastOne.
claims.note: The commodity lines group states no upper limit on the number of lines.

claims.statement: Every commodity line must carry a commodity code.
Every commodity line must carry a species Latin name.
A commodity line's species common name is optional.
Every commodity line must carry a number of animals.
A line's number of packages is asked only when that line's commodity code is in the package-count list, and even then it is optional.
The county parish holding number is asked, and mandatory, when any commodity line's code is in the CPH-required list, and is out of scope otherwise.
Whether the consignment contains unweaned animals is asked once for the whole notification, and only when any commodity line's code is in the unweaned list.

Each animal identifier record inside a commodity line must carry at least one of seven identifiers: a microchip, a passport, a tattoo, an ear tag, a horse name, identification details or a description; an empty record is refused under obligation.unitRecord.identifiersRequired.

The at-least-one-identifier floor is stood down unless more than one commodity line has a code in the identified list, so a consignment with a single identified line is not held to it at the collection level.
claims.quote:
floorAppliesToParent: moreThanOne(
      allowListed(commodityCode, identifiedCommodityCodes, null)
    )
---
 * The inner gate names the entries that would be asked; this wrapper stands
 * the whole rule down unless there are at least two of them, and otherwise
 * hands back the inner decision untouched with the same `fulfilmentIndexes`.
claims.note: mechanism: works on the commodity-lines collection. moreThanOne returns the inner allowListed decision only when it admits more than one entry, and otherwise reports out of scope.

claims.statement: A microchip is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the microchip list, and is optional there.
A passport is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the passport list, and is optional there.
A tattoo is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the tattoo list, and is optional there.
An ear tag is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the ear-tag list, and is optional there.
A horse name is asked of an animal only when its line's commodity code and species Latin name together are in the horse-name list, and is optional there.
claims.quote:
export const horseName = {
  id: HORSE_NAME_ID,
  name: 'horseName',
  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'optional',
  applyTo: allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    horseNameCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,
    [horseNameReason]
  )
}

claims.statement: Identification details are asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and are optional there.
A free-text description is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and is optional there.
A permanent address is asked of an animal, and is mandatory, when its line's commodity code and species pair is in the permanent-address list.
claims.quote:
const permanentAddressPairGate = (reasons) =>
  allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    permanentAddressCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,
    reasons
  )

export const permanentAddress = {
  id: '3fcbd0e6-f708-4c2c-89ab-a56c7e8ea0b7',
  name: 'permanentAddress',
  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'mandatory',
  applyTo: permanentAddressPairGate([permanentAddressReason])
}
claims.note: The only mandatory per-animal identifier obligation; every other one is optional.

claims.statement: Where that permanent address came from is asked on the same animals as the permanent address itself, and is optional.

claims.statement: A trader can attach between zero and fifteen accompanying documents to a notification, and a sixteenth is refused under obligation.accompanyingDocument.tooMany.
The fifteen-document cap is enforced on the stored notification as well as on the page's Add affordance, so a saved notification holding more than the cap is still caught afterwards.
Each accompanying document must carry its own type, attachment type, reference and date of issue; all four are mandatory within a document.
A document's upload id and filename are optional, so a document can be recorded without a file attached.
The V4 data dictionary page still reads as if a notification can hold at most one accompanying document, and the obligation model is treated as the authority until that page is amended.
claims.note: An existing ruling recorded in code: a known disagreement with the V4 source, resolved in favour of the model.

claims.statement: Each document's instance id is a session-scoped counter value such as doc1 or doc2.
claims.quote: // Instance ids are session-scoped counter values (`doc1`, `doc2`, …).

claims.statement: A gate that reads one stored answer and swaps the mandate keeps the answer in scope on both branches, while one that swaps in scope drops the stored answer when the gate answer flips.
claims.quote:
Both
 * `whenTrue` and `whenFalse` are returned verbatim, so a caller who
 * passes two in-scope decisions gets a pure status flip (e.g.
 * `regionCode` mandatory ↔ optional), and one in-scope + one
 * out-of-scope gets a purge-on-flip (e.g. `purposeInInternalMarket`
 * dropped when `reasonForImport` changes).

claims.statement: A per-line or per-animal gate decides entry by entry, so one commodity line can be asked for an identifier while another in the same consignment is not.
claims.quote:
/**
 * allowListed — in scope on entries where `gateObligation`'s stored
 * value is in the allowlist.
 *
 * - Depth-1 (gate + gated at the same identity level): pass `null` for
 *   `gatedParentGroup`; fulfilmentIndexes are the passing gate keys.
 * - Depth-N > 1 (gate broader than gated): pass the gated obligation's
 *   parent group as `gatedParentGroup`; fulfilmentIndexes are that
 *   group's fulfilmentIndexes whose ancestor prefix has a passing gate.

claims.statement: An answer that is blank never counts as outside an allowlist, so a commodity line with no code yet is not treated as an unidentified species.
claims.quote:
/**
 * notInUnionOf — dual of `allowListed`. In scope on entries whose
 * `gateObligation` stored value is not blank and not in the union of the
 * given allowlists. The union is derived at call-time and exposed on
 * `.metadata.values`.

claims.statement: A trader searching for a commodity gets one page of species grouped by CN code, with the total, the page number and the page size alongside.
claims.quote:
/**
 * One page of the species matching a term, grouped by CN code.
 *
 * @param {string} term - the search term.
 * @param {{page?: number, size: number}} paging - the zero-based page and its size.
 * @returns {Promise<{total: number, page: number, size: number, groups: Array<{code: string, species: Array<{latinName: string, commonName: string|null}>}>}>} the page of results.
 * @throws {import('@hapi/boom').Boom} 503 when reference data fails.
 */

claims.statement: The commodity search asks the reference data service for GET /commodities with the search term as q and the page and size as query parameters.
The species check asks the reference data service for POST /commodities/species-check with the commodity lines in the body.
claims.quote:
export const checkSpecies = (lines) =>
  requestReferenceData(
    referenceDataUrl('/commodities/species-check'),
    { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ lines }) },
    'Failed to check species'

claims.statement: The species check returns the commodity lines whose Latin name is not listed under their commodity code, and an empty list when every line's species is listed.
claims.quote:
/**
 * @param {Array<{code: string, latinName: string}>} lines - the lines to check.
 * @returns {Promise<Array<{code: string, latinName: string}>>} the lines whose
 *   Latin name is not listed under their code; empty when all are listed.
 * @throws {import('@hapi/boom').Boom} 503 when reference data fails.
 */

claims.statement: No species check is made at all when there are no commodity lines to check.
A species-check reply that carries no unlisted list is treated as a failure rather than as 'nothing unlisted'.

When the service is run in stub mode both the commodity search and the species check are answered from the service's own fixtures instead of reference data, and stub mode is never honoured in production.
A reference data failure is turned into a 503 'Reference data unavailable' naming the dataset that failed, either 'commodities' or 'species'.
Every call to reference data carries the service's trace headers and a JSON content type, and any non-OK reply is raised as a failure carrying the status, status text and URL.

Six commodity codes carry per-animal identifiers: cattle 0102 (ear tag, passport, tattoo), horses 0101 (microchip, passport and a horse name for Equus cabalus), swine 0103 (ear tag, tattoo), sheep 010410 (ear tag), goats 010420 (ear tag) and other live mammals 01061900 (microchip, passport, tattoo).
Those same six codes are the identified list, so a commodity line with any other code is treated as unidentified and asked for identification details and a description instead.
claims.quote: export const IDENTIFIED_CODES = Object.keys(COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS)

claims.statement: The horse name is asked only for the species named Equus cabalus under commodity code 0101.
claims.quote:
export const HORSES_CODE = '0101'
...
const HORSE_NAME_SPECIES = 'Equus cabalus'
...

Horses (0101) ask for a package count but do not require a CPH number; the three 0407 egg codes require a CPH number but ask for no package count.

claims.statement: Five commodity codes raise the unweaned-animals question: horses 0101, cattle 0102, swine 0103, sheep 010410 and goats 010420.

  HORSES_CODE,
  CATTLE_CODE,
  SWINE_CODE,
  SHEEP_CODE,
  GOAT_CODE
]

claims.statement: Only three species need a permanent address, all under commodity code 01061900: Felis catus, Canis familiaris and Mustela putorius furo.
claims.note: Cats, dogs and ferrets, in Latin.

claims.statement: Commodity code 01061900 is the one code whose species are listed individually rather than as a single commodity.

---

claims.statement: Four commodity codes carry a description: 0101 'Live horses, asses, mules and hinnies', 0102 'Live bovine animals', 01061900 'Other live animals' and 0301 'Live fish'.
Three commodity codes carry a short name: 0101 'Horse', 0102 'Cattle' and 0301 'Fish'.
Live fish, commodity code 0301, has a description and a short name but no identifiers, so a fish consignment is asked for identification details and a description rather than a tag or passport.
claims.quote: export const LIVE_FISH_CODE = '0301'
claims.note: 0301 is absent from COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS, so it is outside IDENTIFIED_CODES and the notInUnionOf gates for identification details and description admit it.

claims.statement: The per-identifier code lists are derived from the one identifier table rather than written out, so a code that carries an identifier is always in that identifier's list.
claims.note: mechanism: turns the identifier table into per-identifier code lists, and into code-and-species pairs for an identifier that names a species.

claims.statement: A commodity search in stub mode matches a group when the term is a prefix of its CN code, and otherwise matches a species when every word of the term is a prefix of consecutive words of its Latin or common name.
claims.note: mechanism: the stub's own matching over the captured commodity fixtures; an empty term matches nothing by name, and a code prefix match returns the group's whole species list.

claims.statement: Stub search results are paged by slicing the flattened matches and then regrouping them by code, so a group can be split across two pages and the total counts species rather than groups.
claims.note: mechanism: paging over the stub's flattened code-and-species matches.

claims.statement: In stub mode a commodity line counts as unlisted when the captured fixtures hold no group with that code carrying that exact Latin name.
claims.quote:
const listedInStub = ({ code, latinName }) =>
  COMMODITY_GROUPS.some(
    (group) =>
      group.code === code &&
      group.species.some((species) => species.latinName === latinName)
  )

export const unlistedLinesInStub = (lines) =>
  lines.filter((line) => !listedInStub(line))

claims.statement: Four answers decide which conditional questions a trader sees, and they are exercised as a cross product of 48 states: whether a region code is required, the reason for import (unanswered, internal market, transit or temporary admission of horses), the means of transport (unanswered or road vehicle) and the transporter type (unanswered, commercial or private).
claims.quote:
/**
 * The scope-determining flags whose cross-product spans the conditional
 * obligations moving into and out of scope: the region-code requirement, the
 * import reason, the means of transport and the transporter type. The reason
 * axis carries transit and temporary-admission values so the reason-gated
 * destinationCountry / portOfExit / exitDate obligations are exercised.
 * 2×4×2×3 = 48 states.
 *
 * @returns {Array<object>} 48 partial answer states.
 */

claims.statement: The journey's reachability is proved over 240 answer states, each of the five seed variants overlaid with each of the 48 scope states, with unanswered values left out rather than stored blank.
claims.note: 5 seed variants × 48 scope states = 240 answer states.

claims.statement: Two answers are the required earlier answers every later page needs before it will open: the country of origin and at least one commodity line.
claims.note: Matches the two obligations named in ENFORCED_AT_CONTINUE, countryOfOrigin and commodityCode.

claims.statement: A test seed for a page that needs a permanent address carries the country of origin as well, because every page's Save and continue needs it before a later page will open.
claims.quote:
/**
 * A consignment of commodity lines that already hold animal identifier
 * records, for a page or a test that needs an animal whose commodity and
 * species pair needs a permanent address. Carries the country of origin
 * every page's Save and continue needs before it will open a later page.

claims.statement: A commodity line's number of animals can be given while its identifiers are not, so the count and the identifier records are recorded independently.
claims.quote:
`numberOfAnimalsQuantity` overrides the count derived from
 * `units.length`, for a line whose count is given while its identifiers are
 * not.

claims.statement: A page's Back link goes to one of five places, decided by the trail: the page Save and continue was pressed on, the overview when the trader came from the overview, the review when they came from a Change link, the review when they came from a Change link while amending, and the overview when the trail names a place the journey does not have or says nothing at all.
claims.quote:
const backCases = ({ previousPage }) => [
...
          'the page Save and continue was pressed on',
...
  [
    'Overview when opened from Overview',
...
  [
    'the review when opened from a Change link',
...
  [
    'the review when opened from a Change link while amending',
...
  [
    'Overview when the trail names a place the journey does not have',
...
  [
    'Overview when nothing says where the trader came from',
    [],
    (journeyId) => hubPath(journeyId)
  ]
]

claims.statement: After a refused save, the page shown again goes Back to the page Save and continue was pressed on, not to the overview.
claims.quote:
/**
 * Registers the Back case of a refused save: the page shown again goes Back
 * to the page Save and continue was pressed on.
 */

claims.statement: A commodity line in a seed is built from a species row that already pairs a commodity code with a Latin name, so a line's code and species are never set independently in a test.
claims.note: mechanism: builds a commodity line from a species row and a count of ear-tagged animals.

claims.statement: A cat line in a seed records a number of animals and no number of packages, so the two counts are not both required of one line.

The set's flow names no page order or sequencing for the notification actions, the amendment or the deletion: the four action slugs are exempted from the entry guard and otherwise sit outside the journey's eight sections.
claims.note: Amend, cancel amend, copy and delete are reachable by URL on any notification whatever its answers, and no section or task row sequences them.

claims.statement: The journey's own section order and the caption groupings disagree in three places: animal identification is captioned 'About the consignment' although the flow puts it in description of the goods, transit countries is captioned 'Movement' although the flow puts it in transport and arrival, and the permanent address page is captioned 'Addresses' although the flow puts it in consignment parties before the addresses page.
claims.quote:
{ id: 'movement', pages: [transitCountriesPage] },
  { id: 'transportAndArrival', pages: [portOfEntryPage, transportersPage] },
claims.note: Recorded as an ambiguity for the reconciler: a page's caption is not derived from the journey section it sits in, so the two lists can drift.
